summary: Compose verified MAX inbound Webhook reception through the public tenant-bound route and host-owned Inbox/outbox replay boundary.

impacts.evidence: The public route derives organization and workspace scope from four fixed URL segments, resolves the account inside that scope and rejects mismatched account bindings before adapter execution.
The typed claim keeps raw provider JSON ephemeral and the durable event stores only bounded normalized IDs and a SHA-256 fingerprint without the verification token.
A new unauthenticated POST route is registered under the fixed webhook prefix with a stable four-segment path; existing authenticated API routes are unchanged.
The additive commerce.social.webhook_received.v1 event has a catalogued JSON Schema and the host publishes only the minimized verified envelope.
SocialWebhookDeduplicator now receives a typed SocialWebhookClaim so every host implementation sees the same normalized delivery metadata and bounded validation contract.
Task-009 inbox_receipts and the existing transactional outbox tables already persist the replay receipt and event; no schema migration is needed.
The route is public by design but always acknowledges uniformly, while MAX performs constant-time secret verification and exact channel, type, MID and timestamp validation before the claim.

The account must be active and explicitly enable the readable social.webhooks capability; the route has no privileged authenticated bypass and durable processing remains bounded to the connector account.
The EventBus event carries a deterministic account-bound event ID, correlation delivery ID and source social-webhook, providing lineage for the Inbox receipt and outbox publication.
Content-addressed delivery identity plus the tenant-scoped Inbox consumer make provider retries duplicate-safe and detect immutable event-ID collisions.
MAX inbound Webhook receipt is admitted through the public route; subscription and unsubscription egress remain outside the application surface and are not overclaimed.
Uniform acknowledgement protects provider retry behavior, structured warning logs expose rejected stages without secrets, and Inbox/outbox failures remain visible for operational retry.
Disabling the account capability or removing the route registration stops new durable claims, while already committed Inbox and outbox evidence remains immutable.
MAX adapter, typed SDK claim, runtime admission, public route, event schema fixture and full contract/Go validation cover success, malformed input, capability denial and tenant binding.
